values.value: In HubSpot, the CRM and the marketing platform are the same product. How much of your customer data model would have to move with the marketing estate — and who else is using it?

[{"value":1,"label":"HubSpot IS the CRM. Sales works in it daily, deals and pipeline live there, and marketing data cannot be separated from it."},{"value":2,"label":"HubSpot CRM is in real use by at least one non-marketing team, and custom objects or properties are shared across them."},{"value":3,"label":"HubSpot CRM holds marketing contacts and properties only; the system of record for customers is elsewhere and syncs in."},{"value":4,"label":"A separate system of record already owns the customer; HubSpot holds marketing attributes that could be re-derived from it."}]
Ask who logs into HubSpot who is not in marketing, and what they do there.

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/skills/02-maturity.md — diagnostic question 6, "Who owns your customer data model?", where the Stage 2 answer is "Marketing owns DEs, CRM team owns CRM, they sync periodically". That question assumes the two are separable; in HubSpot they are one product, so the base slot's question ("is the data model knowable and mappable") is not a harder or easier version of the right question, it is a different question. SUBSTITUTION RATIONALE (required for layer 3): the slot keeps position 5 and keeps its risk theme — whether the audience/data layer can be moved — but the thing that makes it risky here is entanglement with another team's system of record rather than the shape of the schema. Rewording the base anchors would have produced a question whose 1 and its 4 described different axes. Slot count, position and 1-4 scale are unchanged, so the total is still out of 32 and still comparable.
